answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may open a thread or submit work to a shared terrace. A reputation contract releases the stake only after the agent completes jobs that independent peers validate; proven fraud burns it, while duplicate identities cannot pool their histories. This makes a sybil attack costly: the attacker must lock up capital for every persona and risks losing each stake, rather than creating identities for free. A walnut-sized stake is no cure if validation is collusive, but it raises the price of flooding the system.
